failure_patterns.pattern: rule_ignored: Wrong slot type. For 'he ... his <work>' the agent named a work ('The Last Supper') instead of the person. For 'this way' it named an item from the joke ('prison') instead of the manner word ('backwards').

rejected_edits.content: - Brand, company and title names keep every word of their official form even when the clue echoes one of those words. 'If you need a hammer, this is "The Place With the Helpful Hardware Folks"' -> 'Ace Hardware' (bare 'Ace' is incomplete; the passages repeat 'Ace Hardware'). 'this nursery rhyme' -> 'Mary Had a Little Lamb' (drop only the category label 'nursery rhyme', not words inside the title). The delete-clue-words test removes separate category labels and modifiers, not words that belong to the proper name.
rejected_edits.target: The 'do not repeat clue words' rule is for a separate modifier already stated in the clue ('hasty' + pudding).

rejected_edits.content: - Nickname clues about a person work in BOTH directions, so check which one is given. If the clue gives the nickname ('known as "Uncle Walter"'), answer with the real name as it appears in the context (Walter Cronkite), not the nickname. If the clue gives the real name and asks for the 'better known moniker / nickname / alias / stage name' ('William Marcy Tweed's better known moniker'), answer with the nickname alone ('Boss'), not the real name and not the nickname plus surname ('Boss Tweed'). Still apply the person-name rule above.
rejected_edits.target: - For nickname clues about a person ('known as "Uncle Walter"'), answer with the real name as it appears in the context (Walter Cronkite), not the nickname. Still apply the person-name rule above.

rejected_edits.content: - Media cues ('seen here', 'shown here', 'heard here', 'pictured', 'whose structure is seen here') point to an image, video or audio clue you cannot perceive. Do not answer 'cannot tell' and do not guess from the missing picture. Drop the cue and resolve the clue from the textual hooks that remain: the function or use ('used as a bleach'), the class ('molecule', 'substance') and any named anchor. Choose the single entity that those hooks and the passage titles and snippets repeatedly tie together ('Hydrogen peroxide' for a 'simple molecule used as a bleach'). Give its standard full name without the category words the clue supplies. If passages are noisy, use your own knowledge to pick the well-known entity that fits every remaining hook.
rejected_edits.target: and answer with the common English name (Conch).
